stories.headline: 10-YEAR YIELD PUSHES BACK ABOVE 5% AS HAWKISH FED REPRICING CONTINUES
stories.body: Two days after the FOMC's quarter-point hike to 3.75%-4.00%, the 10-year Treasury yield climbed roughly 6 bps to 5.01%, closing out a losing week for stocks even as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both ticked higher Friday.
stories.explain: Wednesday's initial move lower in long yields reflected skepticism that the hiking cycle would stick; today's reversal back above 5% shows that skepticism fading as the market digests Fed officials' signal that at least one more hike is likely before year-end. When investors raise their expected path of future short rates, the 10-year's pricing formula — expected average short rate plus term premium — pushes higher even without any new Fed action that day.

stories.headline: S&P 500, NASDAQ 100 EKE OUT GAINS BUT STILL POST WEEKLY LOSSES ON RATE JITTERS
stories.body: The S&P 500 rose 0.17% to 7,650 and the Nasdaq 100 climbed 0.67% to 29,644 on Friday, but both indexes still finished the week lower as the 10-year yield's return to 5% kept pressure on valuations.
stories.explain: A single day's bounce doesn't undo a week's worth of discount-rate math: when the rate used to value future corporate cash flows rises, present values of those cash flows fall, hitting long-duration growth stocks hardest. Friday's modest gain reflects some dip-buying and short-covering, but the weekly net loss shows the market still repricing for a Fed that means what it said about more hikes.

stories.headline: WTI FALLS THIRD STRAIGHT SESSION TO $100 AS SAUDI PIPELINE FEARS EASE
stories.body: WTI crude dropped 1.6% to roughly $100 a barrel while Brent slipped 0.9% to about $103.87, with both benchmarks finishing the week essentially flat as traders concluded Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline outage will dent supply less than first feared.
stories.explain: WTI and Brent are priced off different supply pools — WTI off U.S. domestic inventories and pipeline flows, Brent off seaborne international cargoes more exposed to Middle East disruptions. The narrowing spread here reflects the market unwinding its initial fear premium: if the pipeline outage reroutes rather than removes barrels from the global market, the risk discount priced into Brent has less reason to persist.

stories.headline: GOLD HITS WEEKLY HIGH NEAR $4,400 AS FALLING OIL COOLS INFLATION EXPECTATIONS
stories.body: Gold rallied about 1.1% to roughly $4,391 an ounce, touching a weekly high near $4,440 intraday, even as nominal Treasury yields ticked higher — a sign investors read this week's oil pullback as taking pressure off the inflation outlook.
stories.explain: Gold is priced off real (inflation-adjusted) yields, not nominal ones, so nominal yields and gold can move in the same direction when inflation expectations fall faster than nominal rates rise. A third straight down session for crude lowers near-term breakeven inflation pricing (the gap between nominal and TIPS yields), which can pull real yields down or flat even while the nominal 10-year pushes back above 5% on Fed-hike repricing.

stories.headline: DOLLAR INDEX HOLDS FLAT NEAR 100.21 AS TRADERS AWAIT NEXT INFLATION PRINT
stories.body: The DXY was essentially unchanged at 100.21, down 0.02%, consolidating just above the psychological 100 level as this week's hawkish Fed hike is already largely priced in.
stories.explain: A currency's level reflects the market's expected interest-rate differential against other major economies over the relevant horizon, not just the most recent policy headline, so a flat DXY here means Wednesday's hike surprise has already been absorbed into forward pricing. This week's core PCE print is the next real catalyst: a hot number would reinforce the case for another hike and likely push the dollar higher, while a soft one could undercut it.

stories.headline: GEORGIA COURT STAYS RJ GODFREY'S ELIGIBILITY, CLOUDING ARIZONA'S ROSTER DAYS BEFORE FIRST PRACTICE
stories.body: The Georgia Court of Appeals stayed the injunction that had let Godfrey and 15 other class-of-2022 seniors compete for a fifth season, making him ineligible again just as college basketball's first official practices open Monday — part of a broader Cobb County lawsuit challenging the NCAA's new 'five-for-five' eligibility rule.

stories.headline: PISTONS RULE OUT RAISING JALEN DUREN OFFER BEFORE CAMP, HARDENING MONTHS-LONG STALEMATE
stories.body: With training camp about two weeks out, Detroit is holding its extension offer near $190 million over five years against Duren's $200 million-plus ask (he's eligible for up to $287 million) and has resisted sign-and-trade scenarios, leaving Duren's clearest path a $9.6 million qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next summer.

stories.headline: PATRIOTS SHUT DOWN AARON RODGERS AND STEELERS 20-3 FOR FIRST WIN OF THE SEASON
stories.body: New England's defense sacked the 42-year-old Rodgers four times and forced a fumble that Eli Ponder returned for a touchdown, while TreVeyon Henderson added a 39-yard rushing score in his season debut as Rodgers finished 23-of-39 for 187 yards with an interception.

stories.headline: TRINIDAD CHAMBLISS LEADS OLE MISS PAST LANE KIFFIN'S LSU 32-24 IN COACH'S RETURN TO OXFORD
stories.body: In Kiffin's first trip back to Oxford since leaving Ole Miss for LSU, Chambliss — the quarterback Kiffin recruited from a Division II program and developed into a star — beat his former coach outright, handing LSU its first loss of the season.

Guard Tayshawn Comer has committed to Washington via the transfer portal, joining fellow transfers LeJuan Watts (Texas Tech, 11.8 ppg) and Harun Zrno (Rutgers) on Danny Sprinkle's retooled roster. Women's team released its full Big Ten-title-hopeful 2026-27 schedule this week.

deepDive.title: Beyond Expected Rate Path: What the Term Premium Adds to a 5% 10-Year Yield
content: Friday's brief closed with the 10-year Treasury back above 5%, driven by markets repricing the Fed's rate path after this month's hike. But 'the market now expects more hikes' only explains part of that move. Bond yields decompose into two pieces: the average expected path of short-term rates over the bond's life, and a term premium — extra compensation investors demand for the risk of holding a long-dated bond through an uncertain rate future. Separating the two tells you whether the bond market is worried about the Fed's path itself, or about the uncertainty surrounding it.

The expectations component is straightforward: if investors think the fed funds rate averages 4.5% over the next decade instead of 4%, the 10-year yield should rise roughly in step, since a 10-year Treasury is economically a bet that rolls over successive short-term rates. The term premium is subtler — it compensates for the risk that realized rates deviate from that expected path, for inflation uncertainty, and for the fact that a 10-year bond's price swings far more per basis point of yield than a 3-month bill's. The New York Fed's ACM model regularly puts the term premium anywhere from slightly negative to over 100 basis points depending on the regime.

What most people miss is that the term premium, not the expected rate path, drove some of the biggest yield surprises in modern history. In the 2013 'taper tantrum,' the 10-year yield jumped roughly 100 basis points in three months even though the Fed hadn't raised short rates at all — it had merely signaled it might slow bond purchases, and the term premium spiked on that uncertainty alone. If today's move above 5% is mostly expectations catching up to a Fed that has said it means business, that is a more stable repricing than if it reflects genuine doubt about where policy heads next.

That distinction matters directly for this week's setup. If the core PCE print comes in hot, an expectations-driven move higher in yields would be fairly proportional to how much more tightening the data implies. But if yields overshoot the number itself, that's the term premium pricing in policy uncertainty, not just a higher rate path — and it tends to unwind faster once clarity arrives. Watching how the 10-year reacts relative to the surprise in the data, more than the print itself, is the cleaner read on which piece of the yield actually moved.
